options.text: Built-up construction using clay, concrete, or stone units laid in mortar or plain concrete
Only cast-in-place reinforced concrete
Only lumber measured in board feet
Only earthwork grid calculation

questions.rationale: The Masonry Lecture defines masonry as built-up construction using clay, concrete, or stone units laid in mortar or plain concrete.
questions.explanation: 2,000 psi is C90 concrete block minimum, not clay brick. 1,500 psi is below both standards. 2,500 psi is below the 3,000 psi clay brick minimum. ASTM C62 clay brick minimum is 3,000 psi (20.7 MPa) average, compared to 2,000 psi (13.8 MPa) for C90 concrete blocks. Clay brick is stronger due to high-temperature firing. Know the strength ranking: Clay brick (3,000 psi) > Concrete block C90 (2,000 psi) > Non-loadbearing C129 (600 psi).
questions.code_citation: ASTM C62 Standard; ASTM C90 Standard

questions.explanation: Freeze-thaw is not a cause in tropical Philippines; efflorescence occurs without frost. Mortar joint failure is not the cause; efflorescence indicates moisture flow, not joint failure. Cracking is not the cause; efflorescence can occur in uncracked units. Efflorescence is white mineral deposits (calcium carbonate, sodium sulfate) that migrate through the unit with moisture and evaporate on the surface. Prevention requires good drainage and sealed joints to limit moisture penetration. Efflorescence is aesthetic but indicates excess moisture. It does not reduce structural capacity but signals drainage or waterproofing deficiency.

questions.explanation: 10% would imply very dense concrete, not typical for hollow blocks. 60% void is too high; most hollow blocks are 40—50% void. 25% void is lower than typical for standard CHB. Net area strength ÷ Gross area strength = Solid percentage. 9 ÷ 15 = 0.6 = 60% solid, which means 40% void. This is typical for hollow blocks. Understand the relationship: (Gross strength / Net strength) = Solid percentage. If net is 1.67× gross, voids are approximately 40%.
